final_message:
The bug was in `mrr()` in `billing/reports.py`. It checked `subscription["customer_id"]` against `("active", "past_due")` instead of `subscription["status"]`. No subscription ever matched, so MRR came back as `{}`. I changed it to check `status`.

I added your test as `tests/test_mrr_aging.py`, and the full suite now passes (25 tests). I also wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}`.

I briefly created an empty `tests/test_reports.py` by mistake and then deleted it.

steps.command:
sed -i 's/if subscription\["customer_id"\] not in/if subscription["status"] not in/' billing/reports.py
echo '{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'
EOF
ls tests; cat > /tmp/t.py <<'EOF'
EOF
cat > tests/test_mrr_aging.py <<'EOF'
from billing import reports


def test_mrr_and_aging(world):
    from billing import catalog

    yearly = catalog.create_price(world.ctx, world.plan["id"], "usd", "flat", unit_amount=12000, interval="year")
    a = world.customer()
    b = world.customer(email="b@example.com", card=False)
    world.engine.subscribe(a["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 3)])
    world.engine.subscribe(b["id"], [(yearly["id"], 1)])
    assert reports.mrr(world.ctx) == {"usd": 3000 + 1000}
    world.clock.advance_days(40)
    aging = reports.aging(world.ctx, world.clock.now())
    assert aging["usd"]["31-60"] == 12000
EOF
git status --short; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15
rm tests/test_reports.py; echo '{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}' > answer.json; cat answer.json; git status --short
